name: The Fathom Line
motto: Below the surface is where the money is.
description:
The Fathom Line is a crew of eighteen divers and underwater demolition specialists who control access to the submerged sections of Milwaukee's old port infrastructure. When lake levels shifted and the harbor district partially flooded, an entire layer of the city went underwater — warehouses, transit tunnels, industrial facilities, and the sealed vaults of businesses that didn't have time to relocate their assets. The Fathom Line makes its living accessing these submerged spaces and extracting what's inside.

Unlike the Lakebed Scrapers in Chicago, who focus on volume salvage, the Fathom Line specializes in precision recovery. They're hired by clients who know that something specific is down there — a sealed data vault, a flooded pharmaceutical stockpile, a cargo container that sank before it could be loaded — and need someone with the equipment and skills to retrieve it. The crew charges by the job, and their rates reflect the danger: cold water, zero visibility, unstable structures, and the constant risk of entrapment in a flooded space where rescue is impossible.

The crew's equipment is a mix of salvaged commercial diving gear, modified industrial tools, and custom-built underwater cutting and welding rigs. Several members run aquatic augments — gill-assist implants that extend dive time, pressure-resistant subdermal reinforcement, and sonar packages that let them navigate in total darkness. These augments are expensive to maintain, which keeps the crew perpetually working to fund their next round of modifications.

The Fathom Line also runs a sideline in underwater disposal. Need something to disappear permanently? The flooded harbor district has thousands of spaces that nobody will ever search. Bodies, evidence, weapons, data — the Fathom Line will sink it for a fee and guarantee it stays sunk.
ideology: The deep belongs to those who dare it. The Fathom Line views the flooded districts as their sovereign territory — ungoverned, unreachable by surface authorities, and full of value that only they can access. They're territorial about their dive sites the way surface gangs are territorial about streets.
territory: Milwaukee's flooded old port district and adjacent submerged infrastructure. Topside base in a converted boathouse on the harbor edge.
methods: Precision recovery — retrieving specific items from submerged locations on commission
Dive operations — extended underwater work in flooded structures using augmented diving capability
Underwater demolition — cutting, blasting, and dismantling submerged structures to access sealed spaces
Disposal services — permanently sinking items, evidence, or bodies in the flooded district
Salvage assessment — surveying submerged sites and selling maps to prospective clients
Territorial enforcement — sabotaging unauthorized divers who enter their waters
resources: Eighteen skilled divers with underwater operations experience
Aquatic augments — gill assists, pressure-resistant subdermals, sonar navigation packages
Salvaged commercial diving equipment and custom underwater tools
Detailed sonar maps of Milwaukee's flooded infrastructure
A converted boathouse base with equipment storage and maintenance facilities
Exclusive knowledge of submerged access points and sealed spaces

story_hooks: A client hired the Fathom Line to recover a sealed data vault — the contents turned out to be encrypted records of a pre-flood corporate massacre
A Fathom diver found a submerged facility that's still powered and still sealed — something is running down there
The crew disposed of something for a client that's now been linked to a high-profile murder — the evidence needs to stay sunk or the crew goes down with it
A rival diving crew is encroaching on Fathom territory, and the resulting underwater skirmishes are escalating
The flooded district is being drained for a corporate development project — the Fathom Line's entire territory and business model is about to disappear
